title: Exact block repetition and unbounded derived direct image
statement:
Let $u:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a geometric morphism of topoi presented by small sites, so $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ with $u^{-1}$ preserving finite limits. Let $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ be sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal Y$, and put $B_i^X=u^{-1}B_i$. For a ring sequence $A$, let $\mathscr S(A)$ denote strict semilinear systems of module sheaves: objects have $A_{i+1}$-linear maps $M_{i+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{A_{i+1}\to A_i}M_i$, and morphisms are compatible componentwise maps. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories, exact component evaluations, levelwise inverse image and its total derived direct image $Ru_{*,A}$ of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].
Let $t:\mathbf Z_{\ge1}\to\mathbf Z_{\ge1}$ be nondecreasing and surjective, with each fiber a finite nonempty interval. Put $a_i=\min t^{-1}(i)$ and $D_m=B_{t(m)}$, with identity ring maps inside each block and the specified $B$-transition between blocks; likewise $D_m^X=B_{t(m)}^X$. Define the repetition functor $R_t^W:\mathscr S(B^W)\to\mathscr S(D^W)$ by $(R_t^WM)_m=M_{t(m)}$, with identity transitions inside each block. Define $E_t^W:\mathscr S(D^W)\to\mathscr S(B^W)$ by $(E_t^WP)_i=P_{a_i}$, using the composite transition from $a_{i+1}$ to $a_i$ and the identification $D_{a_i}=B_i$.
Then $E_t^W\dashv R_t^W$, and both functors are additive and exact. The component at $m\in t^{-1}(i)$ of the adjunct of $f:E_t^WP\to M$ is $P_m\to P_{a_i}\xrightarrow{f_i}M_i$. In particular $R_t^W$ preserves K-injective complexes (a complex $I$ is K-injective when every map from an acyclic complex to $I$ is chain homotopic to zero).
There is a canonical natural isomorphism on ordinary unbounded derived systems
$$\kappa_t:Ru_{*,D}R_t^X\xrightarrow{\sim}R_t^YRu_{*,B}.$$
On any K-injective $B^X$-system representative $I$, it is the identity comparison of the two identical complexes $(u_*I_{t(m)})_m$, under the canonical derived-functor identifications. These normalization equations determine $\kappa_t$ independently of resolutions, including its map action and transitions. Together with the strict inverse-image identity $u_D^{-1}R_t^Y=R_t^Xu_B^{-1}$, this comparison intertwines the units and counits of the derived geometric adjunctions. The comparison is natural in the coefficients: let $b:B\to B'$ be a compatible map of ring sequences on $\mathcal Y$, with $b^X=u^{-1}b$, repeated sequence $D'_m=B'_{t(m)}$, repeated maps $d_m=b_{t(m)}:D_m\to D'_m$, $d^X_m=b^X_{t(m)}$, and exact restrictions of scalars $U_b,U_d$, so that $R_t^WU_{b}^W=U_{d}^WR_t^W$ strictly. Let $\beta_b:U_b^YRu_{*,B'}\to Ru_{*,B}U_b^X$ and $\beta_d:U_d^YRu_{*,D'}\to Ru_{*,D}U_d^X$ be the comparisons of total right derived functors induced by the strict identities $U\,u_*=u_*U$ through the universal property of the right derived functors. Then $$\kappa_t^{B}U_b^X\circ\beta_dR_t^X=R_t^Y\beta_b\circ U_d^Y\kappa_t^{B'}$$ as maps $U_d^YRu_{*,D'}R_t^X\to R_t^YRu_{*,B}U_b^X$. For two block maps, the comparison for their composite equals the composite of their comparisons under strict reindexing identifications; the identity block map gives identity. If $u$ is an open localization, exact extension by zero also commutes with repetition, by the strict identity $j_{!,D}R_t^X=R_t^Yj_{!,B}$, and this identity is compatible with the same reindexings.

proof.text: Use the actual finite-block constructions and coefficient identifications of [lem-pur-system-block-constructions]. Use the actual ringed sequence-site definitions of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. First endpoints a and the block map t form an adjunction a ⊣ t on the sequence site: the unit has index i ≤ t(a(i)) = i, and the counit has index a(t(m)) ≤ m. Both have identity vertical components. The triangle identities hold by thinness of the index category and the identity vertical maps. Apply Mathlib SheafOfModules.pushforwardPushforwardAdj to the endpoint and repetition ring identifications. For its counit ring equation, cancel the invertible repetition identification and use its naturality; after applying t the counit is an equality transport because t(a(t(m))) = t(m). The unit ring equation is also a composition of equality transports. The resulting module-sheaf unit at (m,U) is precisely the transition P_m(U) → P_(a(t(m)))(U), so Adjunction.homEquiv_unit gives the asserted adjunct formula. Composition of continuous pushforwards and equality of their coefficient maps gives the component evaluation isomorphism, identity on section carriers. Endpoint module objects are the original modules after transport along the endpoint ring equality. Reindexing is additive; it preserves finite limits after the forgetful functor to abelian presheaves and finite colimits after the conservative exact functor to abelian sheaves, since the sequence-site reindexing is cocontinuous. This proves every field of SystemBlockRepetition except K-injective preservation.

proof.text: Apply the proved source-library lemma CategoryTheory.Adjunction.preservesKInjectiveComplexes to the exact additive endpoint adjunction constructed in step 1. Explicitly, an acyclic repeated-system complex H remains acyclic under endpoint evaluation E. A map H → R(I) transposes to E(H) → I; K-injectivity of I makes it null-homotopic, and the additive degreewise adjunction transports this homotopy back. Thus repetition preserves K-injectives without any assertion that individual evaluations preserve them. Exact termwise descent is the existing construction of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization].

proof.text: Use [lem-pur-block-geometric-core] for the repeated ordinary inverse-image system P, direct core K, and normalized squares. Use [lem-pur-block-geometric-adjunction-assembly], proved by applying the already proved [lem-coef-ordinary-direct-system-hom-data] to the local transition-mate core K: this assembles the global Hom equivalence from the component adjunctions. Prove left and right naturality of that equivalence by ordinary evaluation and the naturality of P.component and K.component, and use Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv to construct the repeated ordinary adjunction. The two normalized evaluation-square equations imply that its Hom equivalence intertwines repetition with the original ordinary Hom equivalence. Apply this identity to an identity map to obtain unit compatibility, and to the original counit, using injectivity of the new Hom equivalence, to obtain counit compatibility. Additivity follows from preservation of binary products for P and from the right-adjoint criterion for K. Apply [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] to the repeated ringed sequence site for Grothendieck abelianness; [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective] supplies K-injective resolutions of this actual repeated system category. Finally [lem-pur-system-block-derived-comparisons] gives canonical normalized derived comparison, uniqueness, derived adjunction compatibility, coefficient naturality and composition/identity coherence.

proof.text: Construct the open-slice repetition evaluation equality by continuous module pushforward composition and its coefficient-map equation; its restriction maps are the original reindexed restrictions. Apply the proved assembly and normalization theorem [lem-pur-block-open-extension-assembly] to these data. That theorem constructs normalized OpenSystems data, assembles the explicit component isomorphisms after checking the horizontal-compatibility obligation, and proves naturality, the full heterogeneous normalization equation, and uniqueness. Exact termwise descent is the existing mapDerivedCategorySquareIso construction. The generic assembly proof is in a support module so both files stay within the compilation limit.
